name: return_without_action
description: The body is only a return with no work, so the routine does nothing when called. Its three callers therefore use it as an empty placeholder.

name: invert_mask_register_bits
description: Returns the bitwise inverse of an input word masked to bits 2 and 3, so the caller receives a two-bit value.

name: reflect_variable_when_masked
description: Calls two helper routines, then tests the high bits of an input word against a fixed mask. When the test passes and a helper returns nonzero, the shared variable is replaced with minus three minus its previous value.

name: store_word_then_reflect
description: Calls a helper, copies an input word into a shared variable, and if any masked high bit is set and a helper returns nonzero, replaces that variable with three minus its value.

name: evaluate_status_mask_adjustment
description: Tests several status masks on a shared variable and returns a word when one pattern matches. Otherwise it compares computed word values, adjusts the shared variable by a constant and sets result flags, calling seven helper routines along the way.

name: match_mode_bits_return_flag
description: Checks a word passed in a register against one of two bit patterns, chosen by whether a shared variable is zero. On a match it stores fixed values into shared variables and returns one, otherwise it returns zero.

name: iterate_object_table_update
description: Walks a 32-entry table of 40-byte records and counts active entries whose type code lies outside two excluded ranges. It calls per-record helper routines for each active record and makes an indirect call through a jump table when a flag is set.

name: multiply_record_byte_by_64
description: Reads the byte at offset one from the record addressed by an address register and returns it multiplied by 64.

name: clear_two_shared_variables
description: Writes zero to two shared variables. The bytes after those stores decode as undecodable data, so only the two clearing steps are recovered.

name: mirror_and_store_object_slot
description: If a flag is set, it temporarily toggles a bit and recomputes the horizontal position around a 320 reference value. It then clips the position and size against fixed bounds and stores the result in the next free slot of a 26-byte record table.

name: clip_and_store_object_slot
description: Clips an object's horizontal and vertical offsets against fixed bounds, then fills the next free slot of a 26-byte record table with its clipped position, size and state. It returns minus one when the table is full.

name: release_entries_inside_window
description: Computes a clamped window around a point and walks a list of three-word entries until a negative marker. Entries inside the window get their third word set to a sentinel and are passed to helper routines chosen by its value, and the routine also touches the background colour hardware register.

name: adjust_object_position_by_size
description: Subtracts half of one size field, less 16, from the x position and the other size field, less 16, from the y position, unless a flag bit is set. When a further field is not one, it calls a helper and copies a masked value into a second record.

name: allocate_object_slot_from_table
description: Searches a 32-entry object table for the first inactive entry and fills it with the position and type values passed in registers, clearing its other fields. It takes one attribute byte from a lookup table and sets the entry's kind to four, or to eight when a flag bit is set.

name: allocate_object_slot_with_pointer
description: Searches a 32-entry object table for the first inactive entry and fills it with register values, including an address value stored as a long word. It clears the remaining fields, takes an attribute byte from a lookup table, and sets the kind to four, or eight when a flag bit is set.

name: offset_position_from_source_record
description: Subtracts half of one source size field, less 16, from the destination x position and the other size field, less 16, from the y position, unless a flag bit in the source is set. When the source's state field is not one, it calls a helper and copies a masked value into the destination.

name: process_object_table_entries
description: Loops over a 32-entry table and dispatches each active entry by its type code range to helper routines, with one exact code value handled separately. It then looks up an offset from a table indexed by the entry's bits to compute a position update, and the routine also touches the background colour hardware register.

name: update_object_state_by_flags
description: Chooses a state for an object from bits in its status word. One branch adjusts its horizontal position by half its size and sets state fields, another sets a field to a fixed value, and the last writes a code made from its low bits plus a base value, calling helper routines in each branch.

name: set_status_code_from_flags
description: Picks a status code from two bits of an object's status word and writes a fixed status pattern with it. The code is then copied into each of the four following fields that are already nonzero.

name: compute_scaled_size_from_byte
description: Sets a shared variable to 32 by default. When a type byte is nonzero, the variable is replaced by a size byte multiplied by 16.

name: update_contact_state_in_window
description: Checks an input flag word and, when the right bits are set, updates an object's state fields depending on whether a horizontal offset falls inside a window of 25 or 16 units. It calls one helper routine first and sets a countdown field to 10 in some cases.

name: apply_window_contact_response
description: Tests whether a horizontal offset from the object's position lies inside a window of 25 or 16 units, and when it does, updates a countdown field and a vertical value. This is the same window test that appears inside the larger contact routine.

name: emit_object_entries_to_list
description: Sets up a few shared values from the object's status flags, then copies up to eight nonzero fields of the object into a list buffer at an offset derived from its position. The layout depends on the object's type byte, and the routine also touches the background colour hardware register.

name: copy_object_fields_to_list
description: Copies an object's fields into a list buffer at an offset derived from its position, with the layout chosen by its type byte. Unlike the preceding routine it does no status-flag setup first, and it also touches the background colour hardware register.

name: retire_object_past_threshold
description: Counts down a timer field on an object, then calls a helper and compares its result with a threshold. Below the threshold it returns unchanged; at or above it, it copies the object's fields into a list buffer and clears the object's first word.

name: remove_object_outside_bounds
description: Checks whether an object's stored list entry still lies within fixed horizontal and vertical bounds around a shared position. If it is outside, the object's first word is cleared and its fields are copied into a list buffer.

name: decode_command_code_byte
description: Decodes a one-byte code from an input word through a chain of comparisons, setting a shared counter or state for each recognised value. It also looks up a table entry and checks three long-word patterns to set a final value, calling two helper routines along the way.

name: store_data_byte_into_record
description: Calls a helper routine, then stores a byte from a data register into a fixed field of the object record addressed by an address register.

name: spawn_object_into_free_slot
description: Finds the first free slot in a 32-entry object table and initialises its fields from register inputs. It then links up to eight frame values from a list buffer into the new object and sets its kind, and if no slot is free it calls a helper and returns.

name: skip_empty_routine
description: The body is a bare return with no instructions, so it does nothing. Its two callers therefore treat it as an empty placeholder.

name: release_table_entries_to_records
description: Walks the 32-entry object table and, for every entry with a nonzero first word, copies that word into the field of its linked record, clears the entry and decrements the active count. It returns the last value copied.

name: advance_countdown_position_step
description: Advances an object's position by a value from a lookup table indexed by its countdown byte, then decrements that countdown. A countdown reaching zero or ten is reset to 255, and a negative status byte on a different object just clears it.

name: dispatch_object_state_handler
description: Reads an object's status word and, when its flag conditions hold, calls a handler selected from a jump table by the word's low five bits. It then updates the object's position and, in one branch, copies its fields into a list buffer.

name: dispatch_object_handler_direct
description: Has the same body as the preceding routine, but is reached through a direct call rather than by taking its address. It selects a handler from a jump table by the status word's low five bits and then updates the object's position.

name: clear_flag_and_toggle_bit
description: Clears the top bit of a status byte at offset 30 in an object record, then flips the lowest bit of the same byte.

name: clip_and_store_indexed_slot
description: Computes a base address from an index register, then, if the record table has a free slot, clips the object's offsets against fixed bounds and stores it there with a fixed size of 32. If the table is full it calls a helper instead.

name: clip_and_store_offset_slot
description: Clips an object's offsets against fixed bounds, adding an offset from an address register into its position, and stores it in the next free slot of a record table with a fixed size of 32 only when the horizontal clip value is zero. If the table is full it calls a helper instead.

name: call_helper_when_zero
description: Calls a helper routine only when a shared variable is zero, then returns zero in all cases.

name: service_interrupt_request_bits
description: Loops over four pending-event flags kept in a shared variable. For each flag that is set it clears the flag and calls a helper if the matching hardware bit is also set, and the routine touches the interrupt request and enable registers.

name: update_countdown_and_place_sprite
description: Decrements a countdown in an object record, then places the object at a position computed from its stored offsets when a field is negative. Once the countdown reaches zero it copies the object's fields, and otherwise it writes a fixed pointer and marker value into a linked record.

name: refresh_linked_record_state
description: Calls three helper routines, then writes a clamped position difference and a fixed value into a linked record. When a shared flag is set it clears it, copies stored values into the record, and sets a state value from further stored values.

name: refresh_linked_record_from_object
description: Writes a clamped position difference and a stored value into the record linked from an object, and when a flag is set, clears it and copies stored values into that record. It does the same work as the preceding routine but reads its inputs from an address register, and the facts list the DMA and interrupt control registers as touched.

name: tick_countdown_and_call_helper
description: Calls three helper routines, then, if a shared flag and a value are both set, decrements a countdown byte and calls a helper when it reaches zero. It returns the value in either case.

name: return_target_after_timer
description: When an object's enable field is set, it returns a target value and calls a helper once a timer byte has counted down to zero. When the enable field is clear it returns the input register value unchanged.

name: advance_three_phase_level_sequence
description: Advances a three-phase level sequence: each phase reads step and target bytes from a data block, moves the stored level toward its target, and moves to the next phase when the target is reached. The current level is written back into the object record.

name: update_four_sound_channels
description: Steps through four channels in turn, each with its own state block, matching the layout of the Amiga's four audio channels. For each channel it counts down note durations and pitch offsets, reads command bytes from a sequence stream and decodes them with a switch on the command value, and the routine also touches the DMA and interrupt control registers.

name: parse_channel_command_stream
description: Stores the first byte of a sound channel's sequence stream as a channel offset, then reads the next command. Ordinary commands initialise the channel's pointers, timers and note value before running the shared four-channel countdown loop.

name: parse_channel_stream_entry
description: Alternate entry into the sound command decoder that starts at the stream's current position. A command value of 128 sets a one-byte channel parameter, and other commands set the channel's note fields before running the shared four-channel countdown loop.

name: start_channel_from_stored_pointer
description: Loads the channel's stored sequence pointer and runs the command decoder from it. Ordinary commands set the channel's note fields and then run the shared four-channel countdown loop.

name: start_channel_with_scaled_length
description: Reads a length byte from the stream, multiplies it by a value taken through a pointer, and stores the product as the channel's duration before running the command decoder. Ordinary commands then set note fields and run the shared four-channel countdown loop.

name: start_channel_with_divided_rate
description: Divides a fixed constant of 750 by a value read from the stream and stores the quotient through a pointer, then runs the command decoder. Ordinary commands then set note fields and run the shared four-channel countdown loop.

name: start_channel_with_summed_length
description: Adds up a run of bytes from the stream, with the count taken from the first byte, and stores the total scaled by a pointer value as the channel's duration. It then runs the command decoder.

name: load_channel_instrument_table
description: Clears two mode bits on a channel, then copies a block of fifteen bytes from a table selected by a stream byte into the channel record and zeroes its counters. It then runs the command decoder, whose ordinary commands set note fields and run the shared four-channel countdown loop.

name: run_channel_command_loop
description: Runs the sound command decoder from a given stream position without any preset parameters. Ordinary commands set the channel's note fields and then run the shared four-channel countdown loop.

name: load_channel_preset_and_run
description: Loads three preset words and two long words from a fourteen-byte table entry chosen by a stream byte into the channel record. It then runs the command decoder, whose ordinary commands set note fields and run the shared four-channel countdown loop.

name: start_channel_from_pointer_table
description: Selects a sequence start address from a pointer table using a stream byte and runs the command decoder from there. Ordinary commands then set note fields and run the shared four-channel countdown loop.

name: copy_word_pair_three_times
description: Copies two word fields of a structure from one pair of offsets to another, repeating the copy three times while stepping the pointer by two bytes each time.

name: copy_word_pair_twice
description: Copies two word fields of a structure from one pair of offsets to another, repeating the copy twice while stepping the pointer by two bytes each time.

name: stub_decompile_timed_out
description: The decompiler timed out, so no body was recovered for this routine. The facts show only that its address is taken by a pointer and that it has twelve instructions, so its behaviour is not named here.

name: apply_patch_list_at_entry
description: Program entry for the SetPatch utility. It calls several Amiga library routines, parses the QUIET, NOCACHE and REVERSE switches, and works through a patch list, with the referenced text covering the Kickstart 2.0 requirement, enabling the data cache and reporting patches that are already installed.

name: copy_code_block_when_flagged
description: Calls a library routine and returns zero if it fails. Otherwise, when a flag bit in a data area is set, it requests a memory block, copies fifty-one words of its own code into it, and calls library routines around the copy, returning one.

name: copy_code_block_without_check
description: Has the same copy as the preceding routine but without its first library check. When a flag bit in a data area is set, it requests a memory block, copies fifty-one words of its own code into it, and calls library routines around the copy.

name: copy_code_block_and_succeed
description: Requests a memory block and, if one is returned, copies fifty-one words of its own code into it and calls library routines around the copy. It returns one whether or not the copy happened.

name: probe_memory_and_set_config
description: Runs only when a flag byte is not the value 127. It steps backwards through up to four words near a fixed high address, checking whether each one refers to its own address, then writes a derived mask into a configuration byte.

name: return_status_bit_three
description: Returns bit three of a status word in a fixed record, giving eight when it is set and zero when it is clear.

name: release_pending_slot_resources
description: Releases a pending resource stored in one field of a record, then walks six pointer slots and releases each nonempty one through a library call, clearing it along with a companion field. It returns one.

name: dispatch_message_by_type_code
description: Dispatches on a message type code. One code with a matching nested marker copies saved values back and clears fields, and another with an empty sub-field goes to a common completion path that clears flags and replies through the exec library. Any other code is passed to a routine reached through an unrecovered jump table.

name: reply_message_after_restore
description: When a nested marker byte equals four, it copies saved values back into the request, clears its fields and replies to the message through the exec library. Otherwise it passes control to a routine reached through an unrecovered jump table.

name: reply_message_without_pending
description: When a pending field is zero, it copies a saved value, clears a flag and replies to the message through the exec library. Otherwise it passes control to a routine reached through an unrecovered jump table.

name: invoke_cia_handler_pair
description: Calls two helper routines that work with the CIA resources named in the referenced text, then returns zero.

name: toggle_record_flag_around_calls
description: Looks up a record through a library call and, when its flag byte is negative, sets that byte to one around a series of library calls and then clears it again. It returns the result of the last library call.

name: stub_single_call_undecoded
description: The decompiler timed out, so no body was recovered. The facts show only two instructions and one call to another routine, so its behaviour is not named here.

name: forward_to_jump_vector
description: Makes a single call through a jump-table entry that passes control straight on to a fixed address elsewhere in memory, then returns.

name: store_device_bounds_and_base
description: Calls a library routine and, if it returns a nonzero structure, saves a pointer to it, a value read from six bytes into it, and the library base in three shared variables. The referenced text names console.device.

name: check_value_in_stored_range
description: Checks whether an input value lies within a lower and upper bound held in shared variables. Inside the range it calls a library routine and, when that returns nonzero, calls a helper and a second library routine; outside it passes control through an unrecovered jump table.

name: forward_to_unrecovered_jump
description: Passes control through a jump-table entry that the decompiler could not recover, so the routine only forwards to that unknown target.

name: check_upper_limit_then_call
description: Checks an input value against an upper limit held in a shared variable. Within the limit it calls a library routine and, when that returns nonzero, calls a helper and a second library routine, and outside it passes control through an unrecovered jump table.

name: store_address_argument
description: Copies the address held in an address register into a shared variable and returns.

name: store_address_into_shared_slot
description: Copies the value in an address register into the same shared variable that the preceding routine writes, then returns.

name: close_library_and_clear_list
description: Closes a library through a stored base record and walks a linked list in that record, calling a library routine with a fixed argument for each node and clearing a node field when the call fails. It then makes two more library calls and returns one.

name: call_two_library_routines
description: Calls two library routines in sequence and returns one.

name: invoke_single_library_call
description: Makes a single library call at a fixed offset and returns.

name: invoke_library_call_entry
description: Makes one library call at a fixed offset and returns. The facts also show a call to another routine, which does not appear in the recovered body.

name: store_offset_from_library_result
description: Chooses one of two constant offsets based on a field of the input record and calls a library routine, with the referenced text naming dos.library. If that returns a nonzero result it stores the result plus the chosen offset in a shared variable.

name: clear_matching_slot_entries
description: Indexes a table of slots by an input register and, when the slot equals a shared stored value, sets two entries at fixed offsets to minus one and returns. Otherwise it passes control through an unrecovered jump table.

name: clear_matching_slot_or_jump
description: Applies the same check as the preceding routine: when the indexed slot matches the shared stored value it sets two entries at fixed offsets to minus one and returns, otherwise it passes control through an unrecovered jump table.

name: check_slot_and_clear_pair
description: Performs the same slot comparison as the earlier routines. When the indexed slot matches the shared stored value, two entries at fixed offsets are set to minus one, and otherwise control passes through an unrecovered jump table.

name: forward_to_unknown_target
description: Passes control through a jump-table entry that the decompiler could not resolve, so the routine only forwards to that unknown target.

name: set_flag_around_library_calls
description: Makes two library calls, sets a shared variable to 64, makes a third library call and returns one. The facts also list the interrupt enable register as touched.

name: store_address_and_return_one
description: Copies the value in an address register into a shared variable and returns one.

name: fill_marker_words_on_change
description: Calls a function through a shared pointer and compares its result with a value cached per index. When the result changes and equals a fixed sentinel, and a per-index pointer is set, it fills 830 longwords of a buffer with an alternating pattern.

name: fill_marker_words_from_entry
description: Enters the same recovered body as the preceding routine, performing the cached-value comparison and the 830-longword fill when the result changes to the sentinel.

name: fill_marker_words_with_helpers
description: Shows the same recovered body as the entries above, while the facts also list a short operation chain and two helper calls that are not in the recovered code.

name: patch_self_offsets_from_library
description: Calls a library routine, with the referenced text naming intuition.library, and if it returns a nonzero value adds that value to two words of the routine's own code, patching them.

name: copy_field_on_matching_ids
description: Copies a long-word field to another field when two fixed identifier values match and a status mask is set, then increments a counter byte in a shared block.

name: copy_field_on_single_id
description: Copies a long-word field when one fixed identifier matches and a status mask is set, then increments a counter byte in a shared block.

name: clear_low_bit_at_pointer
description: Clears the lowest bit of a long word at a fixed low address, or at a pointer returned by a library call when a flag bit in a shared block is set. It then makes one more library call.

name: scan_list_under_forbid
description: When its address argument is zero, it forbids task switching, scans a linked list for an entry whose 16-bit value matches the input, and permits task switching again before returning.

name: scan_list_with_empty_call
description: Has the same body as the preceding routine. The facts also list a call to an empty stub routine that does nothing.

name: scan_list_from_entry
description: Enters the same body as the preceding routines and scans a linked list for a matching 16-bit value while task switching is forbidden.

name: scan_list_entry_two_calls
description: Shares the same body as the preceding routines. The facts list two unnamed helper calls on this entry.

name: scan_list_entry_on_a1
description: Shares the same body as the preceding routines, but tests a different argument register before it forbids task switching and scans the list.

name: scan_list_a1_variant
description: Shares the argument-tested body of the nearby list-scan routines. It forbids task switching, scans a linked list for a matching 16-bit value, and permits task switching again.

name: scan_list_return_two
description: Forbids task switching, scans a linked list for a matching 16-bit value, and permits task switching again. It then returns the input value if a final check is nonzero, or two otherwise.

name: scan_list_entry_return_two
description: Has the same body as the preceding routine, including the return of two, and the facts list two unnamed helper calls.

name: scan_list_return_minus_one
description: Returns minus one at once when its input is minus one. Otherwise it forbids task switching, scans a linked list for a matching 16-bit value, permits task switching again, and returns the input or minus one depending on a final check.

name: scan_list_minus_one_variant
description: Has the same minus-one check and list scan as the preceding routine. The facts also list a call to an empty stub routine that does nothing.

name: scan_list_input_or_zero
description: Forbids task switching, scans a linked list for a matching 16-bit value, and permits task switching again. It then returns the input value or zero, depending on a final check.

name: scan_list_entry_return_zero
description: Forbids task switching, scans a linked list for a matching 16-bit value, permits task switching again, and returns zero by default.

name: scan_list_return_argument
description: Forbids task switching, scans a linked list for a matching 16-bit value, and permits task switching again. It returns its argument or the input register value, depending on a final check.

name: permit_then_return_argument
description: Makes a library call that permits task switching, then returns its third argument. A final nonzero check makes it return a stack value instead.

name: search_table_for_key_word
description: Gets a pointer from a fixed location, or from a library call when a flag bit is set, then scans forward through words until one matches a stored key. It stores the position it reached, makes one more library call and returns one. The referenced text reads NsDOS Open.

name: dispatch_pointer_unless_opcode
description: Reads the 16-bit word at a stored code address. When that word differs from a fixed processor branch opcode it calls the code there indirectly, and otherwise it calls the routine's own code.

name: dispatch_pointer_entry_check
description: Has the same opcode check and indirect call as the preceding routine. The facts also list two unnamed routines it calls.

name: call_single_routine_and_return
description: Makes one call to another routine and then returns.

name: copy_string_into_allocated_buffer
description: Calls a library routine, then measures a string and allocates a buffer for it through the exec allocation calls. It copies the string in backwards with its length in front, frees the buffer if allocation fails, and otherwise passes control through a library call at a fixed offset.

name: copy_string_backwards_with_length
description: Measures a string and copies it backwards into a buffer whose address is in a register, storing the length in front and a zero terminator at a position taken from a stored byte. It then makes a library call at a fixed offset.

name: copy_bytes_backwards_into_buffer
description: Copies a run of bytes backwards from one buffer to another, storing a fixed byte near the end and a zero terminator at a stored position. It then makes a library call at a fixed offset.

name: stub_empty_return
description: The body is a bare return with no instructions, so the routine does nothing when called.

name: call_library_return_registers
description: Makes one library call at a fixed offset and returns the two registers it leaves behind, so the caller receives those values unchanged.

name: process_count_and_unlink_nodes
description: Increments a counter byte in a shared block and decrements a count field in a record. When the count reaches zero it unlinks nodes from a list, sending a signal through the exec library for nodes with a flag bit set, and then makes a Permit call.

name: adjust_count_or_permit
description: When the negative flag is set it raises an exec alert and initialises a semaphore, and otherwise it decrements a count field in a record. It then makes a Permit library call.

name: alert_then_init_semaphore
description: Raises an exec alert, initialises a semaphore through the exec library, and then makes a further library call. The referenced text names exec.Alert and exec.InitSemaphore.

name: dequeue_nodes_and_signal
description: Removes the first node from a list in a record and, when a flag bit is set on it, repeatedly increments a counter, sends a signal through the exec library and moves along the list. It ends with a Permit call.

name: signal_flagged_list_nodes
description: Walks a linked list in a record from its head, incrementing a counter and sending a signal through the exec library for each node whose flag bit is set. It stops at the end of the list and then makes a Permit call.

name: clear_flag_when_count_ready
description: Increments a counter byte in a shared block and a count field in a record. When the count is nonzero and a pointer is set, it clears one flag bit in a referenced byte, makes two library calls and then a Permit call. Otherwise it increments another field and makes the Permit call.

name: clear_flag_when_slot_set
description: When a pointer field in the record is nonzero, clears one flag bit in a referenced byte, makes two library calls and then a Permit call. Otherwise it increments a count field and makes the Permit call.

name: check_stack_bounds_then_call
description: Compares a stack address with lower and upper bounds stored in a task structure, and also checks a status word for minus one. When any of those conditions holds it calls a handler through a shared pointer and returns the byte it gives back.

name: check_stack_bounds_and_call
description: Makes the same stack-bounds and status check as the preceding routine and calls the shared handler when it fails. It returns no value.

name: check_stack_bounds_variant
description: Repeats the stack-bounds check of the preceding routines with a different handler pointer, and returns the byte from that handler when a check fails.

name: check_stack_bounds_variant_call
description: Repeats the stack-bounds check with a different handler pointer and calls that handler when a check fails. It returns no value.

name: store_two_registers_return_one
description: Copies the value in an address register and a second register value into two shared variables, then returns one.

name: stub_timed_out_single_call
description: The decompiler timed out, so no body was recovered. The facts show three instructions and one call to another routine, so its behaviour is not named here.

name: stub_undecoded_eleven_instructions
description: The decompiler timed out, so no body was recovered. The facts show eleven instructions, a call to a two-instruction helper and one more routine, so its behaviour is not named here.

name: copy_sixteen_longs_then_call
description: Copies sixteen long words from a fixed offset in a block into a caller-supplied buffer when that buffer pointer is nonzero. It then makes an indirect call through a stored pointer.

name: run_if_command_entry
description: Program entry for the If command. It computes a maximum from a list of values, fills a block with a fixed pattern of long words, and calls a function pointer several times. It returns zero on success or minus one on failure.

name: copy_sixteen_longs_variant
description: Has the same copy-and-indirect-call body as the routine at the same offset in the endcli file, copying sixteen long words into a caller's buffer when the pointer is nonzero.

name: run_loadwb_program_entry
description: Program entry for the LoadWB command. It allocates a process record, opens dos.library and the exec resources, parses the command line into words that handle quotes and star-escapes, and waits on its message port. The referenced text includes NIL: and dos.library.

name: release_loader_resources
description: Stores a parameter in a slot of the current loader state and releases resources through conditional library calls: a close call when one field is set, a forbid and reply-message pair when another is set, and a memory free at the end. It returns the stored parameter.

name: launch_resident_tool
description: Checks the command line for a debug option, opens icon.library and related libraries, and starts a resident tool through a helper. The referenced text covers a missing resident tag and a tool that cannot be started, and a global string is XORed with a fixed key in two passes.

name: compare_strings
description: Compares two null-terminated strings byte by byte. It returns minus one when the first string sorts before the second, one when it sorts after, and zero when they are equal.

name: copy_list_into_new_nodes
description: Walks a source list whose nodes link through their first word, allocating an eight-byte node for each entry and copying the entry's value into it. The new nodes are chained together and the head is returned, and the routine stops early if an allocation or copy fails.

name: pad_version_string_on_match
description: Compares a version text in a register with a global string. When the byte at offset 20 is the digit two and the whole global string matches, it overwrites five bytes at offset 17 with a dot and four spaces. Otherwise it advances through the text while it matches the global string. The referenced text reads Workbench release 1.2.

name: write_dot_padding_bytes
description: Writes a dot followed by four spaces into five consecutive bytes starting at offset 17 of a buffer addressed by an address register.

name: match_global_prefix
description: Compares a global string with a buffer byte by byte, advancing through both while they match and stopping at the end of the global string or at a mismatch. It returns no value.

name: stub_empty_routine
description: The body is a bare return, so the routine does nothing when called.

name: forward_with_stack_pointer
description: Calls another routine with its two parameters and a pointer to a fixed stack slot, then returns.

name: format_and_forward_text
description: Calls a formatting library routine, measures the length of the resulting 140-byte stack buffer, and passes the buffer and its length to another routine when that length is nonzero. The library call is RawDoFmt.

name: run_version_program_entry
description: Program entry for the Version command. It allocates a process record, opens dos.library and the exec resources, parses the command line into words in the same way as the LoadWB entry, and waits on its message port.

name: release_version_resources
description: Stores a parameter in a slot of the current program state, then closes a library, forbids task switching and replies to a message, each conditionally, before freeing the state memory. It returns the stored parameter.

name: check_library_version
description: Parses the command line for a library or device name with optional version and revision thresholds, opens it, and compares its version and revision with the given values. It prints a usage or diagnostic message when a check fails, and the referenced text covers the Kickstart and Workbench version lines and an open error.

name: call_flag_then_finish
description: Calls one routine with its first argument and the fixed value 128, then calls a second routine with its second argument and returns.

name: parse_integer_string
description: Parses a decimal string into an integer, accepting an optional plus or minus sign followed by digits, and negates the result for a minus sign.

name: compare_strings
description: Compares two null-terminated strings byte by byte. It returns minus one when the first string sorts before the second, one when it sorts after, and zero when they are equal.

name: calculate_string_length
description: Returns the length of a null-terminated string by walking it until the terminator is found and subtracting the start address.

name: invoke_reschedule_library_call
description: Makes one library call, Reschedule, through a stored library base and returns.

name: invoke_dispatch_library_call
description: Makes one library call, Dispatch, through a stored library base and returns.

name: forward_with_stack_slot_variant
description: Calls another routine with its two parameters and a pointer to a fixed stack slot, then returns. It repeats the forwarding routine in the loadwb file.

name: invoke_allocmem_library_call
description: Makes one library call at a fixed offset, the AllocMem memory allocation routine, and returns its result.

name: invoke_closelibrary_call
description: Makes one library call, CloseLibrary, through the stored library base and returns.

name: invoke_openlibrary_call
description: Makes one library call, OpenLibrary, through the stored library base and returns.

name: format_and_forward_text_variant
description: Calls the RawDoFmt library routine, measures a 140-byte stack buffer, and passes the buffer and its length to another routine when the length is nonzero. It repeats the routine of the same name in the loadwb file.

name: store_byte_at_address
description: Writes the low byte of the data register to the memory address held in an address register.

name: run_hdinstall_entry
description: Program entry for the HDinstall tool. It runs a fixed sequence of helper calls and a loop that calls FreeMem three times, clears a word in a shared record, and swaps one table entry with a RAM variable when it matches a fixed constant.

name: decrement_until_minus_one
description: Decrements a local word until it reaches minus one, then returns.

name: copy_memory_and_forward
description: Calls the CopyMem library routine, then passes control through an unrecovered jump table. It is the entry of the RAM handler program.

name: return_zero_value
description: Returns zero and does no other work, so the routine reports zero without side effects.

name: run_detroit_entry
description: Program entry for the Detroit program. It makes the same kind of helper calls as the HDinstall entry, runs a loop that calls FreeMem three times, clears a word in a shared record, and swaps one table entry with a RAM variable when it matches a fixed constant.

name: decrement_until_minus_one
description: Decrements a local word until it reaches minus one, then returns.

name: depack_backward_bitstream
description: Unpacks compressed data: it reads a bit stream from the end of the input, copies literal bytes and back-references in reverse into the output, and runs three passes. The facts also show a cache-clearing library call when a stored size is large enough.

name: decode_backward_copy_step
description: Part of the same backward unpacker. It reads bits from the input and copies runs of bytes in reverse, with decoded counts kept in shared variables. The facts list only two instructions here, but the decompiled body is the unpacker's bit-stream code, so this follows that body.

name: decode_backward_bitstream_loop
description: Main loop of the backward unpacker. It reads bits and copy counts from the end of the input, writes literal bytes and back-references into the output buffer in reverse, and loops until the stream ends.

name: stub_bad_instruction_data
description: Copies one byte from one address register to another, then the following bytes decode as bad instruction data, so only that copy is recovered.

name: run_zappata_entry
description: Program entry for the zappata program. It calls several helper routines, makes a FreeMem library call, clears a word in a shared record, and returns a pair of register values.

name: increment_counter_clear_bit
description: Library code that increments a 16-bit counter at offset 32 of a structure and clears bit three of a flag byte at offset 14. It returns no value.

name: decrement_library_refcount
description: Library code that decrements a 16-bit reference counter at offset 32 of a structure. When the counter reaches zero and bit three of the flag byte is set, it calls a cleanup routine and returns its result, otherwise it returns zero.

name: unlink_node_or_mark_pending
description: Library code that either unlinks a node from a doubly linked list and frees it through FreeMem, returning a stored value, or, when a pointer field is set, marks the node's flag byte with bit three and returns zero.

name: mark_flag_bit_return_zero
description: Library code that sets bit three of the flag byte at offset 14 of a structure and returns zero.

name: return_zero_library_stub
description: Library code whose body is a bare return of zero, so it does nothing beyond reporting zero.

name: store_result_or_alert
description: Library code that saves an argument and the library base into a structure, calls a library routine at a fixed offset and stores its result. A zero result raises an exec alert, and a nonzero result copies two values into shared variables. The referenced text names dos.library.

name: copy_two_longs_to_globals
description: Library code that copies two long words from offsets 34 and 38 of a structure addressed by a register into two shared variables.

name: forward_to_routine_entry
description: Library code that makes one call to another routine and then returns.

name: forward_to_routine_entry
description: Library code that makes one call to another routine and then returns, with no other work.

name: call_library_handler
description: Library code that simply calls another routine and then returns.

name: forward_to_helper_entry
description: Library code that makes one call to a helper routine and then returns. The helper's purpose is not visible in this body.

description: Library code that calls another routine and then returns, performing no other operation.

name: update_data_field
description: Library code that calls a library routine through a base taken from offset 34 of its first argument, then stores the second argument into the field at offset 148 of the returned pointer.

name: chain_two_calls_with_cleanup
description: Library code that calls one routine with its last two arguments and, when the result is nonzero, calls a second routine with the first two arguments and that result. If the second call fails it calls a cleanup routine and returns zero, otherwise it returns the first result.

name: fill_record_from_stack_buffer
description: Obtains a record through a helper call, reads a second structure into a stack buffer through another helper, and copies its ten long words and several fields into the record. It links the record back through a pointer field when that is set and returns the record. If the read fails it calls a cleanup routine and returns zero.

name: copy_record_fields_from_stack
description: Copies ten long words and several fields from a stack area into a record addressed by a register, and links the record back through a pointer field when that pointer is set.
